title: On the Mystery of Numbers
english: Faith is the thing that is directed toward God, being intangible, beyond comprehension, unseen, unmanageable, and unassailable, silently honored, and worshipped in the mind; for it is the soul's foundation, life's living root, an unfading branch, the fruit of immortality, the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen, and the justification of all the holy.

The Trinity, which is simple, uncompounded, unmixed, unutterable, inexplicable, and indissoluble, consists of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; the Trinity is of the same substance in all things, according to harmony, according to power, according to energy, according to divinity, and according to magnitude in subsistence, yet only divided in name, while being united in power and in works.

The Trinity existed before the ages, without beginning, without end, without decay, without death, without limitation; it neither deserves nor lacks anything, always remaining the same as itself, and it is not newly found, but always worshipped, proclaimed by the apostles, and magnified by the faithful Church, for it is almighty, all-seeing, the Creator, loving, good, unhindered, and perfect.
Even the number of the Trinity itself, as set forth in the Holy Scriptures, is a mystery and a wonder.
The three cherubim sing: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord' (Isaiah 6:3).
Three are the great elements: heaven, earth, and sea; and three are those in us: mind, spirit, and word.
Three were the fathers: Adam, Seth, and Enoch; and three were the patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Three angels appeared by the tent of Abraham.
Three were the days of Abraham's sacrifice; and Sarah, having received the angels, set before them three measures of fine flour.
Jacob peeled three rods and set them in the watering troughs; after three decades of years, Joseph became king.
Moses was hidden by his parents for three months; and three times three, nine plagues of the Egyptians.
Three months after leaving Egypt, the law was written and the stone tablets were brought out; and three are the good things of the wilderness: water, quail-meat, and manna.
Three, he says, seasons Moses appeared before the Lord; and three were the priests: Moses, Aaron, and Samuel.
Three were the mighty commanders: Joshua son of Nun, Caleb Jephunneh, and Phinehas; and three stood against the Amalekites upon the rock: Moses, Joshua, and Hur.
Three were the mighty judges: Gideon, Jephthah, and Samson; and three were the elders of the sons of Israel: Moses, Job, and Daniel.
Three weeks was Daniel's fast; and three boys, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, did not worship the golden image.
By three things the earth trembles, as Solomon said (Proverbs 30:21-23): if a servant becomes king, if a fool is filled with food, or if a hateful woman happens to a good man.
Three things are never satisfied (Proverbs 30:15-16): Sheol, the lust of a woman, and cracked earth.
Three things are beyond tracing (Proverbs 30:18-19): the track of an eagle in flight, the way of a serpent on rock, and the path of a ship in the sea.
Three things go prosperously (Proverbs 30:29-31): a lion's cub stronger than beasts, a rooster walking among hens, and a he-goat leading the flock.

Three wise women—the woman of Tekoa, the Shunammite woman, and Abigail—each demonstrated wisdom: the first rescued the man Nabal, the second rescued Absalom by craft, and the third, having run to the son of the prophet and not having ignored him, saved him.
Three women were prophetesses and tambourine-players: Miriam, Deborah, and Judith; and three holy women: Sarah, Rebekah…
